findings.summary: Gitleaks does not keep the generated config text, so the planned memo key has nothing to read it from.
findings.evidence: I read the struct: it holds only `bin` and `dir`. Gitleaks::new writes generated_config(...) to dir/config.toml and throws the string away. scan_text (line 199) sees only &self and text. Fix: Say that Gitleaks gains a field holding the generated config string, filled in by new(), and that the memo key is built from bin, that string and the text. Do not re-read config.toml on every scan.

findings.summary: The memo test checks that results are equal but never checks that the memo was used, so it would pass even if scan_text skipped the cache.
findings.evidence: The plan compares scan_text with scan_text_uncached and checks clean text after secret-bearing text. A scan_text that never touched the memo would pass every one of these assertions. Fix: Also assert that an entry is in the memo after the first scan, for example a test-only memo length or lookup. Then the test shows the memo stored and returned the findings, not only that the output is unchanged.

findings.summary: The planned timeout test is the same as the existing a_check_past_its_deadline_is_killed test.
findings.evidence: checks.rs:418-441 already runs `sleep 30` with a 300 ms timeout and asserts it did not pass and the note contains "deadline". Fix: Make the new timeout test add something: assert exit_code is None and that elapsed time is close to the timeout (for example under 2 s). Or check that a deadline that falls mid-backoff is not overshot by more than one capped sleep.

findings.summary: The plan offers stashing as a way to get the before timing. It should simply time the untouched tree first.
findings.evidence: The approach says "stash the two code changes, or run the timing first". Step 2 already times the untouched tree before any edit, so stashing is never needed. Fix: Remove the stash option. Time the untouched tree before any edit, as Step 2 says. Record how many runs were made, and whether the target directory was warm or cold, for both before and after.
findings.location: Steps 2 and Approach ('stash the two code changes')

findings.summary: State that the first sleep is 5 ms and that the delay resets for each check, so it is not shared between checks.
findings.evidence: The delay is per call to run_check. A static or shared counter would carry state between checks. Fix: Keep the delay as a local variable inside run_check, and say so in the plan.

summary: The plan matches the request and the accepted reading. The two code changes are in the right places: Gitleaks::scan_text in secrets.rs line 199, and the fixed 200 ms sleep in run_check in checks.rs line 204. I read both functions, and the parts the plan says stay the same (deadline, kill switch, try_wait) do stay the same. Keying the memo by exact text, together with the binary and the config, means two different texts can never share findings. Caching only successful scans and adding no new crate keeps the work within the four files. The timing method is honest: before and after are measured on the job's machine, the earlier jobs' figures are labelled as prior measurements, and if the full test run cannot be done the plan says so instead of inventing numbers. Each criterion has a runnable cargo or git command. I found no blockers and no majors. The minor findings: Gitleaks has no field holding the config text, which the memo key needs; the memo test should show the memo was actually used; the timeout test repeats an existing one; and the plan should time the untouched tree first instead of stashing. Two full cargo test --locked runs of roughly 8 to 12 minutes each (an estimate from the prior figures) should fit in one producer run.
